title: Why Boeing’s Top Airplanes Keep Failing

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片做DJ的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，陈列着这些精美的、已有50年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Questions have swirled for weeks over what went wrong on an Alaska Airlines flight where a piece of the plane blew out into the sky,
sentences.zh: 几周以来，关于阿拉斯加航空一架航班上发生的问题，各种疑问层出不穷，当时飞机的一块部件在空中脱落，

sentences.en: terrifying passengers and renewing concerns about the plane's manufacturer, Boeing.
sentences.zh: 吓坏了乘客，并重新引发了人们对飞机制造商波音公司的担忧。

sentences.en: Last week in Washington, we started to get some answers.
sentences.zh: 上周在华盛顿，我们开始得到了一些答案。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Sydney Ember explains.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事悉尼·恩伯来为大家解读。

sentences.en: It's Monday, February 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月12日，星期一。

sentences.en: Sydney, welcome to the show.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，欢迎来到节目。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: So, Sydney, last month, there was this terrifying incident on an Alaska Airlines flight.
sentences.zh: 那么，悉尼，上个月阿拉斯加航空发生了一起可怕的事故。

sentences.en: A door fell off the plane while it was in midair.
sentences.zh: 飞机在飞行途中掉了一扇门。

sentences.en: And since then, there's been this kind of laundry list of unanswered questions about what went wrong.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，关于到底出了什么问题，出现了一长串悬而未决的疑问。

sentences.en: And ultimately, you know, who was responsible for that?
sentences.zh: 归根结底，你知道，谁该为此负责呢？

sentences.en: And so, last week, we started to get some of our first clear answers.
sentences.zh: 所以，上周我们开始得到了一些初步的明确答案。

sentences.en: But let's start with the accident itself.
sentences.zh: 但我们还是先从事故本身说起吧。

sentences.en: Walk us through what happened.
sentences.zh: 请为我们梳理一下当时发生了什么。

sentences.en: So, Boeing has been under the microscope for about five years after two crashes in late 2018 and early 2019 killed nearly 350 people.
sentences.zh: 波音公司在2018年底和2019年初发生两起空难，导致近350人丧生后，已经处于显微镜下被审视了大约五年。

sentences.en: And these planes, which are Boeing 737 MAX 8 planes.
sentences.zh: 而这些飞机，就是波音737 MAX 8机型。

sentences.en: Important plane for Boeing and for airlines in the United States, right?
sentences.zh: 这对波音和美国各航空公司来说都是非常重要的机型，对吧？

sentences.en: Extremely important.
sentences.zh: 极其重要。

sentences.en: This had become one of Boeing's best-selling planes.
sentences.zh: 这已经成为波音最畅销的机型之一。

sentences.en: You know, it was flying all around the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它在世界各地飞行。

sentences.en: And these crashes cost Boeing billions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 而这些坠机事故让波音损失了数十亿美元。

sentences.en: And it vowed to make the MAX 8s much, much safer.
sentences.zh: 波音发誓要让MAX 8变得更加、更加安全。

sentences.en: But then, this incident in January happens.
sentences.zh: 但随后，一月份就发生了这起事故。

sentences.en: This time with a MAX 9.
sentences.zh: 这次是MAX 9机型。

sentences.en: On January 5th, Alaska Airlines flight 1282 takes off from Portland International Airport heading to Ontario, California.
sentences.zh: 1月5日，阿拉斯加航空1282号航班从波特兰国际机场起飞，前往加利福尼亚州的安大略市。

sentences.en: And about 10 minutes after takeoff, at about 16,000 feet, You just hear a big boom.
sentences.zh: 起飞约10分钟后，在约16000英尺的高空，你只听到一声巨响。

sentences.en: There's a loud bang.
sentences.zh: 一声巨大的爆炸声。

sentences.en: It was silent for, like, one second.
sentences.zh: 大约沉默了一秒钟。

sentences.en: And then you would just feel and hear a lot of air going around, freezing full of air.
sentences.zh: 然后你就能感觉到并听到周围有大量的空气涌入，充满了冰冷的空气。

sentences.en: The plane rattles.
sentences.zh: 飞机剧烈震动。

sentences.en: The oxygen masks drop.
sentences.zh: 氧气面罩掉落。

sentences.en: Lights flicker.
sentences.zh: 灯光闪烁。

sentences.en: So, at first, I thought it was just the window.
sentences.zh: 起初，我以为只是窗户的问题。

sentences.en: And then I realized it was the whole panel.
sentences.zh: 后来我意识到是整个面板都掉了。

sentences.en: Passengers start realizing there's a giant hole now in the plane.
sentences.zh: 乘客们开始意识到飞机上现在有一个巨大的洞。

sentences.en: Maybe a major of the emergency in your intentions.
sentences.zh: 也许是你们意图中的重大紧急情况。

sentences.en: Seattle, Alaska.
sentences.zh: 西雅图，阿拉斯加航空。

sentences.en: 12-A-2, district presser.
sentences.zh: 1282航班，宣布紧急状态。

sentences.en: We're declaring emergency.
sentences.zh: 我们正在宣布紧急状态。

sentences.en: We need to defend them.
sentences.zh: 我们需要返航。

sentences.en: God, that is terrifying.
sentences.zh: 天哪，那太可怕了。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a really, really scary moment for a lot of passengers.
sentences.zh: 是的，这对许多乘客来说是一个非常、非常恐怖的时刻。

sentences.en: I think a lot of them are thinking the worSt.
sentences.zh: 我想他们很多人当时都做好了最坏的打算。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.en: The pilots eventually make an emergency landing back in Portland.
sentences.zh: 飞行员最终在波特兰进行了紧急迫降。

sentences.en: And what had happened was a panel called a door plug.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是一个被称为“舱门塞”的面板脱落了。

sentences.en: That panel had fallen off the plane, essentially.
sentences.zh: 本质上，那个面板从飞机上掉了下来。

sentences.en: There are no serious injuries, but it could have been catastrophic if this had happened at cruising altitude, roughly 30,000 feet or higher up,
sentences.zh: 虽然没有造成严重伤亡，但如果这发生在巡航高度，也就是大约30000英尺或更高的地方，后果可能是灾难性的，

sentences.en: especially if passengers hadn't been wearing their seatbelts or if people had been moving around, as they often are when planes get up to cruising altitude.
sentences.zh: 特别是如果乘客没有系好安全带，或者像飞机达到巡航高度时人们经常做的那样在走动的话。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So really kind of miraculous that no one was actually hurt.
sentences.zh: 所以没有人受伤真的是个奇迹。

sentences.en: I mean, they were pretty close to getting into a zone where there could have been some pretty serious injuries.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们当时离进入可能造成严重伤害的区域非常近。

sentences.en: So what's the reaction to this?
sentences.zh: 那么对此有什么反应呢？

sentences.en: I mean, aside from the obvious terror of the passengers.
sentences.zh: 我是说，除了乘客们显而易见的恐惧之外。

sentences.en: Well, the question immediately is who is to blame.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最直接的问题是谁该负责。

sentences.en: Is it Alaska Airlines?
sentences.zh: 是阿拉斯加航空吗？

sentences.en: Is it Boeing?
sentences.zh: 是波音吗？

sentences.en: Is it Spirit Air Systems, which built the body of the plane and then shipped it to Boeing's factory in Renton, Washington?
sentences.zh: 是制造了机身并将其运往华盛顿州伦顿波音工厂的势必锐航空系统公司（Spirit AeroSystems）吗？

sentences.en: Is it the FAA and federal regulators?
sentences.zh: 是美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）和联邦监管机构吗？

sentences.en: No one really knows in the immediate aftermath.
sentences.zh: 在事发后的第一时间，没人真正知道。

sentences.en: And as these questions are swirling, what happens almost immediately is the Federal Aviation Administration, the main regulator for airlines,
sentences.zh: 当这些疑问四起时，几乎立刻发生的事情是，作为航空公司主要监管机构的美国联邦航空管理局，

sentences.en: grounds MAX 9 planes with this door plug.
sentences.zh: 停飞了装有这种舱门塞的MAX 9飞机。

sentences.en: So it amounts to about 170 MAX 9 planes in this country.
sentences.zh: 这相当于该国约170架MAX 9飞机。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And that seems like a lot, right?
sentences.zh: 这听起来很多，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, the two airlines in the United States that fly MAX 9s at this point are just Alaska and United Airlines.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，目前美国运营MAX 9的两家航空公司只有阿拉斯加航空和联合航空。

sentences.en: But these are, you know, sizable portions of their fleet.
sentences.zh: 但这些飞机在他们的机队中占有相当大的比例。

sentences.en: Alaska has 65 MAX 9s and United has 79, the most of any U.S.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加航空有65架MAX 9，联合航空有79架，是目前美国所有航空公司中拥有最多的。

sentences.en: carrier at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以这打乱了他们的航班时刻表。

sentences.en: So this snarls their schedules.
sentences.zh: 飞行员和空乘人员无法到达下一个目的地。

sentences.en: Pilots and flight attendants can't get to their next destination.
sentences.zh: 他们无法回家，因为他们原本要执飞的飞机被停飞了。

sentences.en: They can't get home because the planes that they were supposed to fly on have been grounded.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个相当庞大的机队数量，承担着繁重的工作。

sentences.en: So it's a sizable number of planes that are doing a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 这对那些航空公司来说成了一个大问题。

sentences.en: And this becomes a big problem for those airlines.
sentences.zh: 那么航空公司自己怎么说？

sentences.en: And what do the airlines themselves say?
sentences.zh: 我是说，特别是阿拉斯加航空。

sentences.en: I mean, specifically Alaska Airlines, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些是波音的客户，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, these are Boeing's customers, right?
sentences.zh: 他们对此有何回应？

sentences.en: How do they respond to this?
sentences.zh: 嗯，航空公司首席执行官们非常强硬地站出来指责波音。

sentences.en: Well, airline CEOs come out pretty forcefully blaming Boeing.
sentences.zh: 我不仅是感到沮丧和失望。

sentences.en: I'm more than frustrated and disappointed.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯加航空的首席执行官说。

sentences.en: The Alaska Airlines CEO.
sentences.zh: 我很愤怒。

sentences.en: I am angry.
sentences.zh: 他说，我很愤怒。

sentences.en: He says, I am angry.
sentences.zh: 我对波音的要求是，他们打算采取什么措施来改善内部的质量管理程序？

sentences.en: My demand on Boeing is what are they going to do to improve their quality programs in-house?
sentences.zh: 此外。

sentences.en: And then in addition.
sentences.zh: 这呼应了许多首席执行官所说的，他们想要追究波音的责任。

sentences.en: This echoes what a lot of CEOs say they want to hold Boeing accountable.
sentences.zh: 他们对波音公司本身感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: They're really frustrated with Boeing itself.
sentences.zh: 一月底，又发生了一件事，给航空公司带来了更多压力，进一步加剧了这种挫败感。

sentences.en: And near the end of January, something else happens that puts some more pressure on the airlines that ramps up the frustration even more.
sentences.zh: 美国联邦航空管理局采取了进一步行动，命令波音限制其所有737 MAX飞机的计划产量增长。

sentences.en: The FAA takes further action and orders Boeing to limit its planned increase in production of all of its 737 MAX planes.
sentences.zh: 帮我理解一下这意味着什么。

sentences.en: And help me understand what that means.
sentences.zh: 所以联邦政府基本上是在说，你们不能再制造这种飞机了。

sentences.en: So the federal government is saying you can't make this plane anymore, basically.
sentences.zh: 联邦政府正在限制波音可以制造的飞机数量。

sentences.en: The federal government is limiting how many planes Boeing can make.
sentences.zh: 这有效地限制了他们每年的飞机产量，以便他们能专注于安全问题。

sentences.en: And this effectively limits how many planes they can produce a year so they can focus on safety.
sentences.zh: 去年年底，他们说每月生产约38架飞机。

sentences.en: At the end of the year, they said they were making about 38 planes a month.
sentences.zh: 他们曾希望今年将产量提高到每月42架，并在2025年进一步提高。

sentences.en: And they had hoped to increase that to 42 planes a month this year and further increase that in 2025.
sentences.zh: 但这在可预见的未来，甚至可能在未来几个月内，都极大地限制了这一点。

sentences.en: But this really limits that for the foreseeable future and possibly for many months.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，联邦政府实际上是在说，我们不信任你们能妥善制造这种飞机。

sentences.en: I mean, the federal government is effectively saying we don't trust you to make this plane properly.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是在说，在你们向我们证明已经解决了质量控制问题之前，你们不能提高产量。

sentences.en: It basically says you cannot ramp up your production until you've proven to us that you've resolved your quality control issues.
sentences.zh: 但即使有这些产量限制，美国联邦航空管理局在检查并认定安全后，仍然批准了之前停飞的MAX 9复飞。

sentences.en: But even with these limits on production, the FAA still clears the previously grounded MAX 9s after inspections and after they're deemed safe to fly.
sentences.zh: 好吧，但此时此刻，你知道，很多矛头都指向了波音。

sentences.en: Okay, but at this point, you know, a lot of fingers are pointing at Boeing.
sentences.zh: 但我们仍然不知道到底是谁该为这次舱门爆裂负责。

sentences.en: But we still don't actually know the answer for who's responsible for this door blowout.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然不知道谁有过错。

sentences.en: We still don't know who is at fault.
sentences.zh: 但在二月初，波音的情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: But in early February, things get worse for Boeing.
sentences.zh: 波音表示，一家供应商在MAX飞机上发现了两个钻孔错误。

sentences.en: Boeing says that a supplier found two misdrilled holes on MAX planes.
sentences.zh: 这将导致他们不得不返工约50架飞机，并可能推迟这些飞机的交付。

sentences.en: And this was going to cause them to have to rework about 50 planes and potentially delay delivery of those planes as well.
sentences.zh: 波音算是提前预判并宣布了这件事。

sentences.en: Boeing sort of got ahead of this and announcing it.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然描绘出波音及其质量控制存在问题的景象。

sentences.en: But it's still painting a picture of something is amiss with Boeing and their quality control.
sentences.zh: 这把我们带到了上周，所有这些事情最终都闹到了华盛顿。

sentences.en: Which brings us to last week when all of this ends up in Washington.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 周二上午，众议院举行了听证会，美国联邦航空管理局局长迈克·惠特克出席了会议。

sentences.en: So on Tuesday morning, there is a House hearing with the FAA's administrator, Mike Whitaker.
sentences.zh: 他说他们将增加在现场的人员，以监督波音的制造过程。

sentences.en: And he says they're going to increase their on-the-ground presence in monitoring Boeing's manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 但他并没有像我认为一些人所预想或希望的那样，就波音问题面临严厉的质询。

sentences.en: But he doesn't face the kind of grilling about Boeing that I think some thought or hoped he might.
sentences.zh: 美国国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）发布了关于那架丢失舱门的阿拉斯加航空飞机的最新信息。

sentences.en: The National Transportation Safety Board has released new information on the Alaska Airlines plane that lost a door.
sentences.zh: 但真正的重磅炸弹是在当天晚些时候，当国家运输安全委员会发布关于该事故的初步报告时投下的。

sentences.en: But the real bombshell comes later in the day when the National Transportation Safety Board releases its preliminary report on the incident.
sentences.zh: 它没有包含所有事情的完整说明，但这是我们对所发生事件的第一个官方快照。

sentences.en: It doesn't have the full accounting of everything, but it is our first official snapshot of what happened.
sentences.zh: 它说了什么？

sentences.en: What does it say?
sentences.zh: 报告里有什么？

sentences.en: What's in the report?
sentences.zh: 像这样的四个螺栓将舱门塞固定在737 MAX 9的侧面。

sentences.en: Four bolts like this one hold the door plug into the side of the 737 MAX 9.
sentences.zh: 顶部有两个，底部有两个。

sentences.en: There are two at the top and two at the bottom.
sentences.zh: 这份报告称，舱门塞上有两对螺栓，本应有助于将塞子固定在机身上。

sentences.en: This report says there are two pairs of bolts on the door plug that was supposed to help hold the plug in place on the plane's body.
sentences.zh: 这是关键信息，因为NTSB正在试图确定为什么那个舱门塞会爆裂脱落。

sentences.en: That's critical information as the NTSB tries to determine why that door plug blew out.
sentences.zh: 看起来它根本就没有正确地连接到机身上。

sentences.en: It appears it simply wasn't at all connected properly to the fuselage itself.
sentences.zh: 它们根本不在那里。

sentences.en: They weren't there.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 报告称，当飞机抵达波音位于华盛顿州伦顿的工厂时，螺栓还在，但当时有一个问题被标记了出来。

sentences.en: It says that the bolts were there when the plane arrived at Boeing's rent-in facility in Washington, but that there had been an issue that was flagged.
sentences.zh: 舱门塞附近有损坏的铆钉，为了修理这些铆钉，必须打开舱门塞。

sentences.en: There were damaged rivets near the door plug, and in order to fix these rivets, the door plug had to be opened.
sentences.zh: 所以它在波音的工厂被打开了，而在那个过程中的某个环节，它被重新装回去时，却没有装回螺栓。

sentences.en: And so it was opened at Boeing's facility, and somewhere in that process, it was put back together, and there were no bolts put back.
sentences.zh: 这看起来是一个非常严重的疏忽。

sentences.en: That seems like a pretty bad oversight.
sentences.zh: 是的，NTSB非常谨慎，没有说明到底是谁做了这件事。

sentences.en: Yeah, and the NTSB is pretty careful not to say who exactly did this.
sentences.zh: 他们没有说谁打开了舱门塞，也没有说谁拆除了螺栓。

sentences.en: They don't say who opened the door plug or who removed the bolts.
sentences.zh: 但显而易见的是，这发生在波音位于华盛顿州伦顿的工厂，这把责任归咎于波音。

sentences.en: But what is clear is this happened at Boeing's facility in Renton, Washington, and that pins the blame on Boeing.
sentences.zh: 即使是波音自己也会说，这发生在我们的制造车间。

sentences.en: Even Boeing itself would say this happened on our manufacturing floor.
sentences.zh: 我们应该承担责任。

sentences.en: We should be held accountable.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些开始让我们得到了关于发生了什么的答案。

sentences.en: So all of this starts to give us the answer to what happened.
sentences.zh: 但我们仍然不知道这是怎么发生的，特别是在波音公司，一家在MAX飞机发生两起空难后已经受到严格审查的公司。

sentences.en: But we still don't know how this happened, especially at Boeing, a company that's already been under scrutiny after the two crashes of its MAX planes.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 太空探索的七十年。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的队伍。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界，并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受nytimes.com/subscribe上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: Okay, so Sydney, we now know the what, what happened, roughly, more or less, but we do not know the answer of how, right?
sentences.zh: 好的，悉尼，我们现在知道了“什么”，发生了什么，大致上，差不多，但我们还不知道“如何”的答案，对吧？

sentences.en: This broader mystery.
sentences.zh: 这个更广泛的谜团。

sentences.en: How could this have happened again at Boeing?
sentences.zh: 波音公司怎么会再次发生这种事？

sentences.en: So help us unpack that.
sentences.zh: 所以请帮我们剖析一下。

sentences.en: Well, there are still truly more questions than answers, but one of the things this incident did was raise more questions about the relationship between Boeing and its regulator,
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实仍然是问题多于答案，但这件事引发的其中一个问题是关于波音公司与其监管机构之间的关系，

sentences.en: the Federal Aviation Administration.
sentences.zh: 即美国联邦航空管理局（FAA）。

sentences.en: In the aftermath of two crashes in five months, U.S.
sentences.zh: 在五个月内发生两起空难后，美国

sentences.en: lawmakers grilled the Federal Aviation Administration about its relationship with Boeing.
sentences.zh: 立法者严厉质询了联邦航空管理局与波音公司的关系。

sentences.en: What we learned after the crashes in 2018 and 2019 was this relationship was really complicated.
sentences.zh: 我们在2018年和2019年的空难后了解到，这种关系确实非常复杂。

sentences.en: A problem with software caused the planes to repeatedly nosedive when it was meant to stabilize the aircraft.
sentences.zh: 软件故障导致飞机在应该保持稳定时反复俯冲。

sentences.en: Those crashes were caused by a flaw in a new software that was supposed to help stabilize the planes.
sentences.zh: 那些空难是由一种本应帮助稳定飞机的新软件缺陷引起的。

sentences.en: An independent investigation has found the FAA itself was not fully aware of a new system on the plane, and the FAA delegated a high percentage of approvals,
sentences.zh: 一项独立调查发现，FAA本身并未完全了解飞机上的新系统，而且FAA下放了很大比例的审批权，

sentences.en: allowing Boeing to certify much of its own work.
sentences.zh: 允许波音公司自行认证其大部分工作。

sentences.en: The FAA handed Boeing the responsibility for determining the safety of that system and basically delegated regulatory authority to Boeing.
sentences.zh: FAA将确定该系统安全性的责任交给了波音，基本上将监管权力下放给了波音。

sentences.en: Like Fox guarding the henhouse type thing.
sentences.zh: 就像狐狸看守鸡舍一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But there is a reason for this.
sentences.zh: 但这是有原因的。

sentences.en: The FAA has limited resources, and they don't have enough people to have enough inspectors on the ground themselves.
sentences.zh: FAA资源有限，他们没有足够的人手在现场进行充分的检查。

sentences.en: And also, building an airplane is really hard.
sentences.zh: 而且，制造飞机确实非常困难。

sentences.en: And the people who know how to do it the best and who know how the plane works the best are the Boeing engineers and Boeing employees who built it.
sentences.zh: 最了解如何制造飞机、最了解飞机运作原理的人，正是制造它的波音工程师和员工。

sentences.en: But this doesn't change the fact that there were actually very few FAA inspectors at Boeing's facility.
sentences.zh: 但这并不能改变波音工厂里确实几乎没有FAA检查员的事实。

sentences.en: Just a small handful compared to the more than 10,000 employees who worked in Renton.
sentences.zh: 与在伦顿工作的1万多名员工相比，这只是极少数。

sentences.en: So, even before the crashes, Boeing employees were starting to blow the whistle about this.
sentences.zh: 所以，甚至在空难发生之前，波音员工就开始为此吹哨了。

sentences.en: Saying the relationship between Boeing and the FAA could cause safety issues.
sentences.zh: 称波音与FAA之间的关系可能会导致安全问题。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a really hard problem, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一个非常棘手的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: I used to write about the drug industry and the Food and Drug Administration, and it was the same thing there.
sentences.zh: 我以前写过关于制药行业和食品药品监督管理局（FDA）的报道，那里也是一样的情况。

sentences.en: You know, a small, tiny handful of inspectors for drug companies with thousands of people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于拥有数千名员工的制药公司来说，只有寥寥几个检查员。

sentences.en: Very difficult to actually police the things when you're the federal government, you're potentially underfunded.
sentences.zh: 当你作为联邦政府，且资金可能不足时，要真正监管这些事情是非常困难的。

sentences.en: Like, the federal inspectors, to some extent, are totally outgunned.
sentences.zh: 就像联邦检查员在某种程度上完全处于劣势。

sentences.en: But there was supposed to be a whole reckoning after those earlier crashes, right?
sentences.zh: 但在那次早期空难之后，本应有一场全面的清算，对吧？

sentences.en: There were lessons that had been drawn at that point about the dangers of this fox guarding the henhouse.
sentences.zh: 当时已经吸取了关于这种“狐狸看守鸡舍”危险性的教训。

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Did anything change?
sentences.zh: 有什么改变吗？

sentences.en: There were some changes after the crashes in 2018 and 2019.
sentences.zh: 2018年和2019年的空难后确实有一些改变。

sentences.en: The FAA took back the authority to determine whether Boeing planes were safe to fly.
sentences.zh: FAA收回了确定波音飞机是否适航的权力。

sentences.en: And so now it's the FAA who determines the airworthiness of Boeing planes.
sentences.zh: 所以现在是由FAA来决定波音飞机的适航性。

sentences.en: There were also some other steps that both Boeing and the FAA took to ensure that this system where the FAA delegates some of the authority for inspections to Boeing works better.
sentences.zh: 波音和FAA还采取了其他一些措施，以确保FAA将部分检查权力下放给波音的系统能更好地运作。

sentences.en: And then in the immediate aftermath of the incident in January of this year, the FAA did start putting more inspectors at Boeing's facility in Renton.
sentences.zh: 然后在今年1月事件发生后的第一时间，FAA确实开始在波音伦顿工厂增加检查员。

sentences.en: In fact, the FAA administrator said he put 20 additional inspectors.
sentences.zh: 事实上，FAA局长表示他增加了20名检查员。

sentences.en: Still, this is not a huge number of inspectors.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，这并不是一个庞大的检查员数量。

sentences.en: But you can see how there would be criticism that the FAA itself doesn't have enough people overseeing Boeing as it should.
sentences.zh: 但你可以看出，为什么人们会批评FAA本身没有像应有的那样拥有足够的人手来监督波音。

sentences.en: OK, so federal inspectors are clearly very outgunned.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以联邦检查员显然处于非常劣势的地位。

sentences.en: But in this case, you know, as we've said, Boeing is really front and center.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，正如我们所说，波音确实处于风口浪尖。

sentences.en: This incident happened at the Boeing factory.
sentences.zh: 这起事件发生在波音工厂。

sentences.en: So my question, I guess, is the same as I had for the federal regulators when it comes to, you know, what's different from those past years.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我的问题和问联邦监管机构的一样，关于过去几年有什么不同。

sentences.en: What changed at Boeing after those big crashes?
sentences.zh: 那些重大空难后，波音发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: Well, after the crashes in 2018 and 2019,
sentences.zh: 嗯，在2018年和2019年的空难之后，

sentences.en: a lot of blame was put on this cultural shift that occurred at Boeing in the 1990s when there was a merger between Boeing and another airplane manufacturer, McDonnell Douglas.
sentences.zh: 很多指责都归咎于波音在90年代与另一家飞机制造商麦道公司合并后发生的文化转变。

sentences.en: And what a lot of people will say is the culture at Boeing shifted from an emphasis on engineering to an emphasis on profits and shareholders.
sentences.zh: 很多人会说，波音的文化从强调工程转向了强调利润和股东利益。

sentences.en: And this is a criticism that you'll hear a lot, especially from old timers at Boeing or former Boeing employees.
sentences.zh: 这是你经常会听到的批评，尤其是来自波音的老员工或前员工。

sentences.en: So after the crashes, Boeing did make a handful of changes.
sentences.zh: 所以空难后，波音确实做出了一些改变。

sentences.en: Its whole leadership changed.
sentences.zh: 它的整个领导层都换了。

sentences.en: Its CEO was fired and the company brought on new board members who had engineering and safety expertise.
sentences.zh: 首席执行官被解雇，公司引入了具备工程和安全专业知识的新董事会成员。

sentences.en: And that was, of course, back then, right after those twin crashes in 2018 and 2019.
sentences.zh: 当然，那是在当时，也就是2018年和2019年那两起空难之后。

sentences.en: What are they saying now about those measures?
sentences.zh: 他们现在对这些措施怎么说？

sentences.en: So they're very clearly saying that all of the changes they implemented after the crashes were not enough,
sentences.zh: 他们非常明确地表示，他们在空难后实施的所有改变都不够，

sentences.en: that this incident on January 5th indicates that they need to still do a lot more.
sentences.zh: 1月5日的这起事件表明他们仍需做更多工作。

sentences.en: And so they've done a few things.
sentences.zh: 所以他们采取了一些行动。

sentences.en: One of the things they've done is they said they would make changes to the quality control processes.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的事情之一是表示将对质量控制流程进行改革。

sentences.en: And that includes at its own factory and also at its supplier's factory at Spirit AerosysteMs.
sentences.zh: 这包括在自己的工厂，以及供应商势必锐航空系统公司的工厂。

sentences.en: And then one of the biggest things they did was when they announced their earnings for the fourth quarter, they suspended their financial guidance for the year,
sentences.zh: 然后他们做的最重要的事情之一是，在公布第四季度财报时，他们暂停了全年的财务指引，

sentences.en: essentially saying this was not the time to focus on financial performance.
sentences.zh: 本质上是说现在不是关注财务表现的时候。

sentences.en: It was a time to focus on safety.
sentences.zh: 现在是关注安全的时候。

sentences.en: So a few moves here by Boeing and a healthy dose of PR, it sounds like, to convince its customers, you know, the airlines, that it's actually focused on safety.
sentences.zh: 所以波音采取了一些举措，听起来还有大量的公关手段，以说服其客户，也就是航空公司，它确实专注于安全。

sentences.en: And do the customers believe it?
sentences.zh: 客户相信吗？

sentences.en: So that's still a little unclear.
sentences.zh: 这还不太清楚。

sentences.en: Some of the airline customers have said publicly that they're sending their own inspectors to Boeing's facility to monitor the manufacturing process.
sentences.zh: 一些航空公司客户公开表示，他们正在派遣自己的检查员到波音工厂监控制造过程。

sentences.en: But at least one CEO, the CEO of United Airlines, has suggested that he might move his business elsewhere to another plane maker like Airbus.
sentences.zh: 但至少有一位首席执行官，即联合航空的首席执行官，暗示他可能会将业务转移到其他飞机制造商，比如空客。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: OK, so that seems quite significant, you know, that customers would potentially be voting with their feet and going to a competitor.
sentences.zh: 好的，这看起来相当重要，你知道，客户可能会用脚投票，转向竞争对手。

sentences.en: Is there any chance that this could actually be existential for Boeing?
sentences.zh: 这真的有可能对波音构成生存威胁吗？

sentences.en: Like that airlines will really start giving their business to Boeing's big competitor?
sentences.zh: 比如航空公司真的会开始把业务交给波音的强大竞争对手吗？

sentences.en: I think that's still a really open question.
sentences.zh: 我认为这仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, remember, Boeing is an American juggernaut.
sentences.zh: 我是说，记住，波音是美国的巨头。

sentences.en: It's a really important company for the American economy.
sentences.zh: 这对美国经济来说是一家非常重要的公司。

sentences.en: And also, there are only two real airplane companies that make these planes.
sentences.zh: 而且，世界上只有两家真正的飞机公司制造这些飞机。

sentences.en: There is Boeing and there is Airbus.
sentences.zh: 一个是波音，一个是空客。

sentences.en: And it's a very complicated process to change how you're going to design your fleets and to pivot if you're unhappy.
sentences.zh: 如果你不满意，想要改变机队设计和转型是一个非常复杂的过程。

sentences.en: These planes take a while to make and a while to deliver.
sentences.zh: 这些飞机的制造和交付都需要时间。

sentences.en: However, you know, Airbus can't possibly make all of the planes and neither can Boeing.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道，空客不可能制造所有的飞机，波音也一样。

sentences.en: So I don't think this is going to be an existential crisis for Boeing at this point.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为目前这不会成为波音的生存危机。

sentences.en: But I think there is mounting frustration.
sentences.zh: 但我认为挫败感正在加剧。

sentences.en: There is the sense of disbelief that you had five years to improve.
sentences.zh: 人们有一种难以置信的感觉，你们有五年的时间来改进。

sentences.en: These really catastrophic crashes happened.
sentences.zh: 发生了这些真正灾难性的空难。

sentences.en: You vowed to do better.
sentences.zh: 你们发誓要做得更好。

sentences.en: Everyone vowed to do better.
sentences.zh: 每个人都发誓要做得更好。

sentences.en: And yet here we are again.
sentences.zh: 然而我们又回到了原点。

sentences.en: And so I do think Boeing has a lot of questions it needs to answer and a lot of reassurance it needs to give customers.
sentences.zh: 所以我确实认为波音有很多问题需要回答，也需要给客户很多保证。

sentences.en: So, Sydney, I'm going to ask you the question that probably a lot of our listeners will have at this point.
sentences.zh: 那么，悉尼，我要问你一个可能很多听众现在都会有的问题。

sentences.en: And that is, should I be worried about flying on one of these planes?
sentences.zh: 那就是，我应该担心乘坐这些飞机吗？

sentences.en: I think this is a question that's front and center for a lot of people right now.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是目前很多人最关心的问题。

sentences.en: But the fact is, you have to remember that flying is incredibly, incredibly safe.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，你必须记住，飞行是非常、非常安全的。

sentences.en: If there hasn't been a fatal accident involving a major U.S.
sentences.zh: 如果过去十多年里没有发生涉及美国大型

sentences.en: airline in more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 航空公司的致命事故的话。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: You're actually statistically more likely to die in a car accident on the way to the airport than you are on the plane.
sentences.zh: 从统计学上讲，你在去机场的路上死于车祸的可能性比在飞机上还要高。

sentences.en: So it is really, really safe to fly.
sentences.zh: 所以飞行确实非常、非常安全。

sentences.en: But I think the fact that you're asking this and others are asking this really could be a problem for Boeing
sentences.zh: 但我认为你问这个问题，以及其他人也在问这个问题，确实可能对波音构成问题，

sentences.en: and really suggests that Boeing needs to solve the safety problems it's having.
sentences.zh: 这也确实表明波音需要解决它所面临的安全问题。

sentences.en: Sydney, thank you.
sentences.zh: 悉尼，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是Wynna Liu。

sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的拼图游戏《Connections》。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Azersky。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called Chromaesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往nytimes.com/games开始今天的游戏吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的消息。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, Democrats went on the defensive to discredit what they said was a partisan hit on President Biden by Special Counsel Robert Herr.
sentences.zh: 周末期间，民主党人采取防御姿态，试图反驳他们所说的特别检察官罗伯特·赫尔对拜登总统进行的党派攻击。

sentences.en: This is a report that went off the rails.
sentences.zh: 这是一份失控的报告。

sentences.en: It's a shabby work product.
sentences.zh: 这是一份粗制滥造的工作成果。

sentences.en: Bob Bauer, the president's personal lawyer, said on CBS Face the Nation that the report was substandard.
sentences.zh: 总统的私人律师鲍勃·鲍尔在哥伦比亚广播公司的《面对全国》节目中表示，这份报告是不合格的。

sentences.en: And so along with the legal conclusion comes this flood of characterizations, factual misstatement,
sentences.zh: 因此，伴随着法律结论而来的是大量定性、事实错误，

sentences.en: pejorative comments about the president that are inconsistent with DOJ policy and norMs.
sentences.zh: 以及对总统的贬损性评论，这些评论与司法部的政策和规范不符。

sentences.en: Herr's report issued last week cleared Biden of wrongdoing in his handling of classified documents, but characterized him as elderly and forgetful.
sentences.zh: 赫尔上周发布的报告排除了拜登在处理机密文件方面的过错，但将其描述为年老且健忘。

sentences.en: The report put a spotlight on what was already a primary concern for voters, Biden's age.
sentences.zh: 这份报告将焦点放在了选民已经非常关心的问题上，即拜登的年龄。

sentences.en: In a New York Times-Siena College poll this fall, more than 70 percent of battleground state voters agreed that Biden was too old to be an effective president.
sentences.zh: 在今年秋季的一项《纽约时报》与锡耶纳学院的民意调查中，超过70%的摇摆州选民认为拜登太老，无法成为一名高效的总统。

sentences.en: At a rally in South Carolina, former President Donald Trump claimed that while he was in office, he told leaders of NATO countries that he would encourage Russia to, quote,
sentences.zh: 在南卡罗来纳州的一次集会上，前总统唐纳德·特朗普声称，他在任时曾告诉北约国家的领导人，他会鼓励俄罗斯，引用：

sentences.en: do whatever the hell they want to countries that he deemed to be in arrears to the alliance.
sentences.zh: “对那些他认为拖欠联盟会费的国家，想干什么就干什么”。

sentences.en: You've got to pay.
sentences.zh: 你们必须付钱。

sentences.en: You've got to pay your bills.
sentences.zh: 你们必须支付账单。

sentences.en: It was an extraordinary claim, suggesting that he was threatening to incite an enemy to attack American allies,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非同寻常的说法，暗示他威胁要煽动敌人攻击美国盟友，

sentences.en: and foreshadowed what could be far-reaching changes in the international order if he wins the White House.
sentences.zh: 并预示着如果他赢得白宫，国际秩序可能会发生深远的变化。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Sidney Harper, Diana Wynn, Mary Wilson, and Claire Tennesketter.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由Sidney Harper、Diana Wynn、Mary Wilson和Claire Tennesketter制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lexi Diao and Michael Benoit, contains original music by Marianne Lozano and Pat McCusker, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由Lexi Diao和Michael Benoit编辑，包含Marianne Lozano和Pat McCusker的原创音乐，并由Chris Wood进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的Jim Brunberg和Ben Landsberg创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter Show》节目，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的建议。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否会因为喝醉而昏睡过去。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on The New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上收听《The Wirecutter Show》。
